top.title: Mercedes’ 652 Points Locked the Constructors’ Title With Three Races Still to Run
top.description: Photo: Steffen Prößdorf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 Stat of the Day: Mercedes now has 652 points, and that was enough to lock up the 2026 Formula 1 constructors’ title with three races still to run. It is the team’s ninth constructors’ championship and its first since 2021, according to RacingNews365’s post-Interlagos standings . Ferrari, second in the table, sits roughly 142 points back with 129 still available. The title was not won on a flashy day. Mercedes scored 22 points in São Paulo with George Russell fourth and Kimi Antonelli fifth, and it was the first time this season that neither car reached the podium. It still needed only to outscore Ferrari by three points, and it did. What the Mercedes constructors title margin reveals Look at where the points come from. Antonelli has 390 and Russell has 262, which add up to the full 652. There is no third scorer to lean on, so the gap to Ferrari is really a gap between two driver pairs. Hamilton has 261 and Leclerc is in the high 240s, so Russell and Hamilton are close to level, as we covered in our look at the one-point gap for third . The 142-point cushion is largely Antonelli’s lead over Leclerc. Photo: Liauzh / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 That matters because Antonelli had already won the drivers’ title in Mexico City a week earlier. Mercedes did not need a perfect weekend in Brazil because one driver had been collecting wins and podiums all year while the other kept the second car in the top five. The weekend that clinched the constructors’ title was the team’s quietest, and it was still comfortable. The rest of the field Red Bull is third on 415 and McLaren fourth on 398, so the order behind Mercedes is Ferrari, Red Bull, McLaren, a long way apart. Max Verstappen is second in the drivers’ table on 279 and extended his lead over Russell in Brazil, helped by his P21-to-P2 recovery, which also exposed a slicks problem at Red Bull . That is a lot of points for a car that is third in the constructors’ standings. What happens next With the team title settled, the remaining races are about second place in the drivers’ standings, the Russell and Hamilton fight, and Ferrari’s pursuit of the runner-up spot. Track action resumes soon, and we laid out what to watch in what the paddock is waiting on . For the latest on the schedule, see The Grid Today for Nov. 12 . How we verified it: The 652-point total, the 22-point Interlagos haul and the three-race margin were cross-checked across GPblog , RacingNews365 and Grande Prêmio . Sources differ slightly on Ferrari’s exact total (510 or 512), so we describe the gap as roughly 142 points. Image credits: Featured image, Photo: Steffen Prößdorf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. top.title: Texas softball nabs Lolo Gamble, Emree Massaad for 2027 class
top.description: Emree Massaad of Johnson reacts after scoring the game-winning run in a game against Bowie. Massaad will play for the University of Texas. (Katy Snell/Photo courtesy of Katy Snell) A pair of Austin-area stars highlights Texas softball's three-player recruiting class for 2027. Head coach Mike White announced Friday that the Longhorns signed catcher Lolo Gamble of Dripping Springs High School, outfielder Emree Massaad of Buda Johnson High School and pitcher Brooklynn Hagerty of Logansport, Ind. All three will join Texas as freshmen next fall. Texas's class ranks No. 12 in the nation by Softball America and No. 18 by D1Softball. MORE: McCombs Field the 'worst stadium' in SEC, but may be expanded, renovated, per Texas coach The 6-foot Gamble, a multi-time All-Centex selection by the American-Statesman, ranks as a composite top-10 national recruit. In Dripping Springs's 2026 season, she helped power the Tigers to the Class 6A Division II championship game after hitting .574 with 23 home runs and 60 RBIs. White said her frame and power will remind Longhorn fans of former All-American Reese Atwood. "Lolo has the tools to be an All-American," he said in a statement. Gamble called Texas her "dream school" growing up in Dripping Springs, which is about 20 miles west of the Texas campus. The 5-3 Massaad, ranked the No. 9 outfielder per Softball America, provides elite play and plenty of speed in the outfield and can also play in the infield, said White. "Emree is a versatile player that will bring speed and defense with her to the Forty Acres," he said. "Equally adept at outfield or infield, the speedster will test infield defenses with her offensive short game." Hagerty, a 5-7 right-hander, ranks as the No. 17 pitcher in the nation for 2027 per Softball America. As a junior in 2026, she went 17-0 in the circle with a 0.63 ERA and 282 strikeouts. She held opponents to just a .083 batting average and .139 on-base percentage. "She has a combination of movement and velocity to get hitters out at the next level," White said. top.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin A political pressure group in Kwara South, Aaro Meta, has urged aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the district to set aside their grievances and support the party’s governorship candidate, Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Salihu Danladi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also backed the emergence of a governorship candidate from Kwara North, arguing that equity, fairness and political balance informed the need for a shift in power to the district. The group’s Coordinator, Engr. Adebayo S. Daramola, made the appeal on Friday while addressing journalists at the News Keg organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin. Aaro Meta said it played an active role in the 2018 O to Ge movement, which contributed to the emergence of the APC-led government in the state in 2019, adding that its position was informed by the need to sustain the party’s political fortunes and promote fairness among the three senatorial districts. The group recalled that during the 2019 governorship election, it supported the emergence of an APC candidate from Kwara Central, despite its base in Kwara South, in consideration of the prevailing political circumstances. That decision, it noted, resulted in the emergence of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, who won the 2019 election and secured a second term in 2023. It urged APC members in Kwara South to demonstrate a similar spirit of political accommodation by supporting Danladi, who hails from Kwara North. “Why can’t we also have a free mind like we did in 2019 to rally support for any candidate that emerged from the Kwara North Senatorial District, rather than having a preferred candidate?” the group queried. Aaro Meta acknowledged that Kwara South had aspired to produce the APC governorship candidate but maintained that political power should be distributed fairly among the three senatorial districts. It argued that since 1999, Kwara South had produced a governor for eight years, while Kwara Central would have accounted for 20 years in office by the time AbdulRazaq completes his tenure in May 2027. The group said supporting a candidate from Kwara North would provide the district an opportunity to produce the state’s next governor. It particularly appealed to aggrieved APC members in Kwara South and members of the G-15 political bloc to embrace reconciliation and work for the success of Danladi and other party candidates in the 2027 elections. “We cannot afford to be a party to the destruction of the house and family we have all toiled to build and nurture all these years, but to always learn to forgive one another when we offend ourselves,” it said. top.description: Aryna Sabalenka had not failed to reach the last four at the WTA Finals since 2021 [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka's season ended in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beat the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals. Sabalenka took her frustration out on her racquet and reacted to losing a point by crouching to the ground at the back of the court as a semi-final place slipped away. The Belarusian was able to force a deciding set after unravelling in the latter stages of the first, but lost the final six games in slumping to a 6-3 3-6 6-1 loss. It came two days after the four-time major winner lost each of the last 11 games as she was thrashed by Mirra Andreeva . Ukraine's 2018 winner Svitolina will meet Czech world number eight Linda Noskova in the last four after finishing runner-up to Mirra Andreeva, who faces Jessica Pegula for a place in Sunday's showpiece. Svitolina is appearing at the tournament for the first time since backing up her triumph by reaching the 2019 final, having this season returned to the top 10 for the first time since 2021. "It was an extremely tough match, especially mentally. I was just trying to play one point at a time," said Svitolina, 32. "This is the tournament where you bring everything to the table and try to play every game as if it's the last." Sabalenka's disappointing 2026 ends Sabalenka had reached the knockout stage at the WTA Finals in each of the past four years [Getty Images] This is the first season since 2022 in which Sabalenka has failed to win a major, losing out in the final at both the Australian Open and the US Open. The 28-year-old claimed three other titles - including completing a rare Sunshine Double with her triumphs at Indian Wells and Miami - and arrived at the Finals with the best win percentage (80.0%, 47-11) on the women's tour this season. However, that was not enough to maintain her position as the world number one, as she was dethroned after 99 weeks by Elena Rybakina following their US Open title showdown in September. Unstoppable at her dominant best, Sabalenka has recorded the most straight-set wins by any player this season (43). She has also won eight of her 13 meetings with fellow top-10 players, with two of those losses coming in major finals against Rybakina, and two arriving this week. While she has remained consistent on the sport's major stages, reaching at least the semi-finals at 13 of the past 16 slams she has contested, she has lost more major finals (five) than she has won (four) over the past four seasons. top.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
top.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. But here’s what hasn’t changed and what needs to change if they’re to have success the rest of the 2026 season: The Raiders still struggle to run the ball consistently and effectively. Defensively, they still struggle to tackle and prevent the big play from biting them. If those two things don’t turn around, it doesn’t matter who the quarterback is. So while it’s easy to fixate on Fernando Mendoza making his first NFL start on Sunday when the Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, the reality is the defense better get some stops against Drew Lock and the Seattle offense and the Raiders better be able to run the ball, whether it’s Ashton Jeanty or Mike Washington Jr. “Yeah, it’s a fair question, and those are things that we’re working on,” Kubiak said Friday when asked about the run game’s struggles. “We work on them all the time in practice. I definitely have seen strides. I know it didn’t show up last week. There’s things that I can do better. There’s things our players can do better. I know team success will come when that area improves on offense and on defense.” At 4-5, the Raiders’ season is far from over. And even with the trading of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota and elevating Mendoza to the starting QB spot, general manager John Spytek insists the team is not throwing in the towel. Nor should they. Win five of the remaining eight games and the Raiders are possibly in the wild card conversation in the AFC. And with the schedule the rest of the way not exactly daunting — yes, the two games vs. the Broncos figure to be somewhat challenging and there’s the trip to Kansas City at the end of the season. But games vs. Cleveland, Tennessee, Arizona and the winless Chargers are certainly winnable. Win those four and find a way to win one of the three against Denver and K.C. and you’re in the picture for the postseason. Of course, a win Sunday against the Seahawks would go a long way toward amplifying the Raiders’ hopes to be playing meaningful football in January. However, the NFL’s stingiest defense awaits the Silver and Black as Seattle allows just 244 yards per game. Kubiak is well aware of that. After all, he was with the Seahawks last year when they went the distance to become Super Bowl champions. And with Sam Darnold out and Lock in at quarterback, maybe we’ll see defensive coordinator Rob Leonard unleash his pass rushers, blitz more and try and get Lock out of rhythm. “We’ve got to execute better, especially to start the game. We’ve got to start faster, and that’s really all about us,” Leonard said of the defense. “What I’m calling a sense of urgency to get lined up, playing with physicality, everybody running to the ball, and it’ll happen. top.description: Ellie McCorkle won two individual titles and Ames placed fifth as a team at the IGHSAU state swimming and diving meet held on Nov. 12-13 at the University of Iowa Campus Recreation and Wellness Center. McCorkle claimed her first individual state championships, winning the 200 and 500-yard freestyle races. She won the 200 freestyle on Nov. 13 with a time of one minute, 48.40 seconds. McCorkle swam a time of 1:50 flat during the prelims to take second to Dowling Catholic's Charlotte Qualley (1:49.21) on Nov. 12, but in the finals she shaved 1.6 seconds off her prelim time, which was just fast enough to edge Qualley's 1:49.63 effort in the finals. McCorkle cruised to victory in the 500 freestyle. She won the prelims of the longest individual race at the meet in 4:57.16, then cut over three seconds off that effort in the finals when she touched the wall in 4:53.93. Cedar Falls' Maelyn Woltz took second to McCorkle in the 500 freestyle with a time of 4:57.90. McCorkle's performance earned her the IGHSAU Athlete of the Year in girls swimming and diving. As a team, Ames scored 150 points. That beat out Iowa City West by nine points for yet another top-five finish for the Little Cyclones, who are in their first season under coach Ben Utesch. top.title: Stewart Cink leads Charles Schwab Cup Championship by 6, plans to stay aggressive
top.description: PHOENIX ― Stewart Cink made a statement on Day 1, backed it up on Day 2 and now Zach Johnson has some work to do. The only two golfers who can win the Charles Schwab Cup are now separated by seven shots heading into the weekend at Phoenix Country Club. Thursday, Cink bolted out to the first-round lead with an 8-under 63 but sputtered a bit early Friday. He opened with a birdie before back-to-back bogeys. A birdie on the fifth was followed by a bogey on No. 6, but another birdie at the ninth led Cink to a front-nine 36. Then, he caught fire, making birdies on all but three holes on the back nine, coming home in 6-under 29. He admitted he didn't even know he shot 29 until he was told during his post-round interview. Cink also admitted to a mid-round funk and to glancing at the scoreboard where he noticed Johnson's score. "I just know I'm a lot better when I'm really detached from the results. I was probably a little bit attached out there," Cink said. "The wind was blowing, and I saw Zach was making this huge run, just making a statement. The same kind of statement I want to be making. But I dig deep, kind of like spiritually and emotionally, like I know when my heart is in the right place for golf, and it's certainly not when I'm trying to wrestle the results to the ground like a bull. You can't do that." Cink's six-shot lead is the largest 36-hole lead on the Champions Tour in 10 years, but he says this is not the time to lay off the gas pedal. "There's no reason to do that. Chris Jones, my caddie, and I, we're very aggressive with our executing, and mostly we're very aggressive with our game plan, too," Cink said. "There's a couple spots where I feel like it's smart and risk assessment to maybe be a little more conservative off the tee, but mostly we're very aggressive. I see no reason to change that because the whole point of the plan is to make the lowest score possible on every hole. I don't care if you're leading by 6 or behind by 6, you still want to continue to try to make the best score on every hole." As for Johnson, he posted a 2-under 69 on Thursday and came out hot Friday, his round sparked by five birdies on his first five holes. After a bogey at No. 7, Johnson tacked on three more birdies at Nos. 9, 12 and 13. He did stumble coming in with bogeys on Nos. 17 and 18, something that left a bitter taste in his mouth. "I hit good shots there early on, it just didn't feel tight," he said after his round, which ended under a light drizzle. "That's probably the best way to put it. I did not feel tight. My game did not feel tidy. My putter was great and I hit some good shots, don't get me wrong. It caught up with me the latter part of the day unfortunately." Johnson is among a four-way tie for third at 7 under with Steve Allen in solo second at 8 under after he shot 69. top.title: Starship flight 15 powers to orbit—setting up a possible catch on Saturday
top.description: STARBASE, Texas—Starship lifted off right on schedule Friday from South Texas, making its 15th test flight in more than three years. The largely successful launch took place in the early evening; as the massive rocket rose into the atmosphere, the Sun sank toward the western horizon. Conditions were ideal for the launch, with the atmospheric winds so calm the rocket’s white plume did not dissipate for many minutes. The weather in South Texas is not always comfortable; summers are long and hot. Friday evening was perfect at Starbase. The first stage ascended toward space flawlessly, releasing the upper stage above the Gulf of Mexico. From there, the Starship upper stage ignited its Raptor engines and powered its way into a nominal orbit. This was the second time SpaceX has flown Starship into low-Earth orbit. top.title: Bambi 2.0: Brajan Gruda’s impressive dribbling stats in Germany debut
top.description: Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images Brajan Gruda produced a number of dazzling displays for RB Leipzig in the opening games of the 2026/27 campaign. Four Bundesliga assists in seven appearances as well as goals in the Champions League and DFB-Pokal were enough to earn the tricky winger a call up to German National Team. Jurgen Klopp even decided to reward Gruda with his debut appearance for Die Mannschaft. He didn’t disappoint. The 22-year-old enjoyed a dream start to his national-team career, scoring a goal in the 50th minute. And it wasn’t just Gruda’s goal-scoring exploits that stood out, it was also his knack for dribbling. According to OptaFranz (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Gruda nearly matched a record set by fellow dribble master Jamal Musiala. Brajan Gruda completed 9 of his 14 dribbles on his Germany debut. Over the past 10 years, only one German player has completed more successful dribbles in a single game: Jamal Musiala, with 13 against Costa Rica at the 2022 World Cup Gruda’s emergence comes at a perfect time. Germany have sorely missed a winger who is competent on the ball and willing to take their man on. Too often the flanks have been timid, leaving the creative and goal-scoring pressure to the central players. The Leipzig attacker’s threat out wide spread the pitch and allowed additional room for Florian Wirtz to operate, a key to Germany’s success. Granted, it was only Serbia. But Gruda’s performance isn’t any less impressive. top.description: Allan Henry-Imagn Images MLB argues its CBA proposal can help ‘address local blackout’ issues appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Major League Baseball is arguing that its proposed changes to the league’s economic system could help eliminate local television blackouts while addressing payroll disparities among its 30 teams. MLB Executive Vice President of Baseball Operations Morgan Sword outlined the league’s position amid ongoing collective bargaining negotiations, identifying television access and competitive balance as two major concerns among baseball fans. “So, what are fans’ biggest issues with baseball today? Two things: one, blackouts. Fans can’t watch the games they want to watch. And second, the game needs to be more fair,” Sword said in a video posted on X, formerly Twitter, by the league. The league’s proposal includes three major changes: splitting baseball-related revenue equally between players and teams, implementing a salary cap and floor, and distributing media revenue equally among clubs. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sword argued that sharing media revenue would reduce financial disparities while giving MLB greater flexibility to address longstanding restrictions on local broadcasts. “First, it will reduce the revenue disparity in baseball and give each team a more equal set of resources to compete with. And secondly, it will finally allow us to address local blackouts, which is something fans have been very frustrated about for a long time,” Sword said. Baseball fans have repeatedly told us they have two issues with the game today: blackouts and fairness We’re proposing to make three major changes to baseball: 1. Entering into a partnership with players where all revenues that are generated are split 50/50 between the teams… pic.twitter.com/GgeKshvFmN — MLB (@MLB) November 13, 2026 Under the proposed salary cap and floor, Sword said 12 teams would increase their spending while eight would reduce theirs. He also pointed to the $446 million difference between MLB’s highest- and lowest-spending clubs as evidence of the financial imbalance. According to Sword, the five highest-payroll teams have averaged 89 wins annually since 1998, compared with 74 for the five lowest-payroll teams. The proposal comes as MLB and the players’ union remain divided over the structure of their next collective bargaining agreement. MLB recently proposed delaying implementation of its salary cap until 2028, with a $258.2 million ceiling and $180.2 million floor. The MLB Players Association has continued opposing a hard salary cap , despite the league’s proposed adjustments. The current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1 , raising concerns about a potential work stoppage affecting the 2027 season. nigeria.title: 2027: Aaro Meta urges Kwara South APC to back Danladi
nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin A political pressure group in Kwara South, Aaro Meta, has urged aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the district to set aside their grievances and support the party’s governorship candidate, Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Salihu Danladi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also backed the emergence of a governorship candidate from Kwara North, arguing that equity, fairness and political balance informed the need for a shift in power to the district. The group’s Coordinator, Engr. Adebayo S. Daramola, made the appeal on Friday while addressing journalists at the News Keg organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin. Aaro Meta said it played an active role in the 2018 O to Ge movement, which contributed to the emergence of the APC-led government in the state in 2019, adding that its position was informed by the need to sustain the party’s political fortunes and promote fairness among the three senatorial districts. The group recalled that during the 2019 governorship election, it supported the emergence of an APC candidate from Kwara Central, despite its base in Kwara South, in consideration of the prevailing political circumstances. That decision, it noted, resulted in the emergence of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, who won the 2019 election and secured a second term in 2023. It urged APC members in Kwara South to demonstrate a similar spirit of political accommodation by supporting Danladi, who hails from Kwara North. “Why can’t we also have a free mind like we did in 2019 to rally support for any candidate that emerged from the Kwara North Senatorial District, rather than having a preferred candidate?” the group queried. Aaro Meta acknowledged that Kwara South had aspired to produce the APC governorship candidate but maintained that political power should be distributed fairly among the three senatorial districts. It argued that since 1999, Kwara South had produced a governor for eight years, while Kwara Central would have accounted for 20 years in office by the time AbdulRazaq completes his tenure in May 2027. The group said supporting a candidate from Kwara North would provide the district an opportunity to produce the state’s next governor. It particularly appealed to aggrieved APC members in Kwara South and members of the G-15 political bloc to embrace reconciliation and work for the success of Danladi and other party candidates in the 2027 elections. “We cannot afford to be a party to the destruction of the house and family we have all toiled to build and nurture all these years, but to always learn to forgive one another when we offend ourselves,” it said. The group warned that internal divisions could give opposition parties an opportunity to gain political advantage, urging APC members not to abandon the party because their preferred aspirants failed to secure its tickets. nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
nigeria.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. nigeria.description: US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain on Friday, a US Air Force spokesperson said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American military aircraft. “No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, the Air Force spokesperson said in a statement. “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added. Nick Timothy, a local member of parliament, said in a statement on Facebook that he had been in touch with authorities at the base and was “told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.” A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.” “Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said. The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base. nigeria.title: Who Gets To Compete?
nigeria.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. nigeria.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. nigeria.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
nigeria.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. business.title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. Home mining is not a profit play Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.title: Mercedes’ 652 Points Locked the Constructors’ Title With Three Races Still to Run
sports.description: Photo: Steffen Prößdorf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 Stat of the Day: Mercedes now has 652 points, and that was enough to lock up the 2026 Formula 1 constructors’ title with three races still to run. It is the team’s ninth constructors’ championship and its first since 2021, according to RacingNews365’s post-Interlagos standings . Ferrari, second in the table, sits roughly 142 points back with 129 still available. The title was not won on a flashy day. Mercedes scored 22 points in São Paulo with George Russell fourth and Kimi Antonelli fifth, and it was the first time this season that neither car reached the podium. It still needed only to outscore Ferrari by three points, and it did. What the Mercedes constructors title margin reveals Look at where the points come from. Antonelli has 390 and Russell has 262, which add up to the full 652. There is no third scorer to lean on, so the gap to Ferrari is really a gap between two driver pairs. Hamilton has 261 and Leclerc is in the high 240s, so Russell and Hamilton are close to level, as we covered in our look at the one-point gap for third . The 142-point cushion is largely Antonelli’s lead over Leclerc. Photo: Liauzh / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 That matters because Antonelli had already won the drivers’ title in Mexico City a week earlier. Mercedes did not need a perfect weekend in Brazil because one driver had been collecting wins and podiums all year while the other kept the second car in the top five. The weekend that clinched the constructors’ title was the team’s quietest, and it was still comfortable. The rest of the field Red Bull is third on 415 and McLaren fourth on 398, so the order behind Mercedes is Ferrari, Red Bull, McLaren, a long way apart. Max Verstappen is second in the drivers’ table on 279 and extended his lead over Russell in Brazil, helped by his P21-to-P2 recovery, which also exposed a slicks problem at Red Bull . That is a lot of points for a car that is third in the constructors’ standings. What happens next With the team title settled, the remaining races are about second place in the drivers’ standings, the Russell and Hamilton fight, and Ferrari’s pursuit of the runner-up spot. Track action resumes soon, and we laid out what to watch in what the paddock is waiting on . For the latest on the schedule, see The Grid Today for Nov. 12 . sports.title: Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals
sports.description: Aryna Sabalenka had not failed to reach the last four at the WTA Finals since 2021 [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka's season ended in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beat the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals. Sabalenka took her frustration out on her racquet and reacted to losing a point by crouching to the ground at the back of the court as a semi-final place slipped away. The Belarusian was able to force a deciding set after unravelling in the latter stages of the first, but lost the final six games in slumping to a 6-3 3-6 6-1 loss. It came two days after the four-time major winner lost each of the last 11 games as she was thrashed by Mirra Andreeva . Ukraine's 2018 winner Svitolina will meet Czech world number eight Linda Noskova in the last four after finishing runner-up to Mirra Andreeva, who faces Jessica Pegula for a place in Sunday's showpiece. Svitolina is appearing at the tournament for the first time since backing up her triumph by reaching the 2019 final, having this season returned to the top 10 for the first time since 2021. "It was an extremely tough match, especially mentally. I was just trying to play one point at a time," said Svitolina, 32. "This is the tournament where you bring everything to the table and try to play every game as if it's the last." Sabalenka's disappointing 2026 ends Sabalenka had reached the knockout stage at the WTA Finals in each of the past four years [Getty Images] This is the first season since 2022 in which Sabalenka has failed to win a major, losing out in the final at both the Australian Open and the US Open. The 28-year-old claimed three other titles - including completing a rare Sunshine Double with her triumphs at Indian Wells and Miami - and arrived at the Finals with the best win percentage (80.0%, 47-11) on the women's tour this season. However, that was not enough to maintain her position as the world number one, as she was dethroned after 99 weeks by Elena Rybakina following their US Open title showdown in September. Unstoppable at her dominant best, Sabalenka has recorded the most straight-set wins by any player this season (43). She has also won eight of her 13 meetings with fellow top-10 players, with two of those losses coming in major finals against Rybakina, and two arriving this week. sports.title: Stewart Cink leads Charles Schwab Cup Championship by 6, plans to stay aggressive
sports.description: PHOENIX ― Stewart Cink made a statement on Day 1, backed it up on Day 2 and now Zach Johnson has some work to do. The only two golfers who can win the Charles Schwab Cup are now separated by seven shots heading into the weekend at Phoenix Country Club. Thursday, Cink bolted out to the first-round lead with an 8-under 63 but sputtered a bit early Friday. He opened with a birdie before back-to-back bogeys. A birdie on the fifth was followed by a bogey on No. 6, but another birdie at the ninth led Cink to a front-nine 36. Then, he caught fire, making birdies on all but three holes on the back nine, coming home in 6-under 29. He admitted he didn't even know he shot 29 until he was told during his post-round interview. Cink also admitted to a mid-round funk and to glancing at the scoreboard where he noticed Johnson's score. "I just know I'm a lot better when I'm really detached from the results. I was probably a little bit attached out there," Cink said. "The wind was blowing, and I saw Zach was making this huge run, just making a statement. The same kind of statement I want to be making. But I dig deep, kind of like spiritually and emotionally, like I know when my heart is in the right place for golf, and it's certainly not when I'm trying to wrestle the results to the ground like a bull. You can't do that." Cink's six-shot lead is the largest 36-hole lead on the Champions Tour in 10 years, but he says this is not the time to lay off the gas pedal. "There's no reason to do that. Chris Jones, my caddie, and I, we're very aggressive with our executing, and mostly we're very aggressive with our game plan, too," Cink said. "There's a couple spots where I feel like it's smart and risk assessment to maybe be a little more conservative off the tee, but mostly we're very aggressive. I see no reason to change that because the whole point of the plan is to make the lowest score possible on every hole. I don't care if you're leading by 6 or behind by 6, you still want to continue to try to make the best score on every hole." As for Johnson, he posted a 2-under 69 on Thursday and came out hot Friday, his round sparked by five birdies on his first five holes. After a bogey at No. 7, Johnson tacked on three more birdies at Nos. 9, 12 and 13. He did stumble coming in with bogeys on Nos. 17 and 18, something that left a bitter taste in his mouth. "I hit good shots there early on, it just didn't feel tight," he said after his round, which ended under a light drizzle. "That's probably the best way to put it. I did not feel tight. My game did not feel tidy. My putter was great and I hit some good shots, don't get me wrong. It caught up with me the latter part of the day unfortunately." Johnson is among a four-way tie for third at 7 under with Steve Allen in solo second at 8 under after he shot 69. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum.
